description: Renovate's output is a pull request, and a pull request runs every validation job; merging to main promotes to deploy only on green (docs/adr/0003-promotion-boundary.md). A bump is therefore reviewable before it can reach the cluster.
What it cannot tell you: whether the bumped chart's pods actually come up. Render and admission checks pass on a chart that crashloops.
BASE: main only. deploy is CI-managed and must never receive a commit that did not pass through main.

argocd.description: Chart pins live in Argo CD Application manifests as `chart:` + `targetRevision:`. The helm-template CI job derives its list from the same files, so a bump and its validation stay in step.

kubernetes.description: Image tags in plain manifests. The trivy CI job scans whatever it finds pinned here, so a Renovate image bump is CVE-checked against its baseline on the same run.

packageRules.description: Patch and minor for the observability stack, grouped. These bump often, rarely break, and reviewing them one at a time is how you stop reviewing them at all.

NEVER group or auto-anything for the storage and policy layers. A Longhorn major is a data-availability event, and Kyverno controls admission for the whole cluster — a bad bump there can lock out every subsequent deploy including its own rollback. Single PRs, and the description says why.
prBodyNotes: :warning: **Storage / policy / PKI component.** The CI gate proves this renders and would be admitted. It does NOT prove the pods come up. Longhorn in particular cannot be validated on the single-node pre-prod (1 replica, no rebuild path). Read the upstream changelog for CRD migrations before merging.

packageRules.description: Majors always separate and never auto-merged, whatever the component.

One minor at a time for cert-manager and Longhorn. Renovate's default proposes the newest minor in one PR, which once proposed cert-manager 1.18 -> 1.21 in one step. Both components carry one-way CRD/engine migrations whose upstream support is minor-to-next-minor only, so each step is its own reviewable PR.
k3s itself is upgraded by system-upgrade-controller from Plans pinned to the running version — NOT by Renovate. Two things bumping the same version is the two-writable-copies problem.
No auto-merge anywhere. Everything here is platform infrastructure for a single cluster with no runtime pre-prod for storage; a human reads every one.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes jump the queue and ignore the weekly window. Pairs with the trivy job's per-image baseline ratchet: this raises the PR, trivy proves the count went down.
